rationale: Both inherited mxalfǝn-wa-nne and supplied mxalfə́n-wa-nne have an explicit -wa; the actor is plural and -nne resumes the sheaves.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (53/26)

data.turoyo: <...> Ya u rabayḏi! Kətlux ḥaq, d qəṭʕət qarʕi, liʔannu ono mxalafli u amrayḏux.
data.translation: <...> Herr, du hast das Recht, mir den Kopf abzuschlagen, weil ich deinem Befehle zuwider gehandelt habe.

rationale: Establishes the missing II Preterit box with a 1sg agent and overt command object.

summary: New box Part act.: example for sense 1b in Part act. (94/304)

data.turoyo: Iḏa kan d oṯe pik w nakkəz aw čək w wəč, hani lanne ḥawrone, mxalfe ne. Hawxa pis kowe, edi komaqəmri.
data.translation: Zeigt der eine Knöchel. die erhabene Breitseite und der andere die hohle Schmalseite (B + C), oder der eine die hohle Breitseite und der andere die erhabene Schmalseite (A + D), so sind das keine Kameraden, sie sind verschieden, der Wurf ist "schlecht", und man verliert.

rationale: First Part act. example for relational subsense 1b; full conditional identifies the two nonmatching faces.

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: intrans. verschieden, nicht zueinander passend (von zwei Stücken; Part act.)

rationale: mxalfe ne explicitly contrasts with 'not companions' for a pair of gaming faces; relational nonmatching differs from disobeying a command. Restricted to the attested predicative form, one occurrence.

data.turoyo: Ono laybi", — omər, — "i ḥaqqiye mxalafna." Omər: "Laybux?" Omər: "Lo!"
data.translation: Ich kann dem, was recht und billig ist, nicht zuwiderhandeln." "Du kannst nicht?" "Nein!"

rationale: Fills II Infectum 1 and preserves the unusual mxalafna spelling in an inability construction.

data.turoyo: Kətli mede medono, qarʕe zalṭono, raġloṯe xəd du dədwono, kmaḥləf əšti noqəṣ ḥa — u šəšwono.
data.translation: Ich weiss' ein Ding mit nacktem Kopf, mit Beinen wie die einer Fliege; es hinterlässt sechzig weniger einen. (Die Ameise; sie hinterlässt Junge).

rationale: Fills III Infectum 1 with an offspring quantity and unusual ḥ spelling; do not normalize it or file it as ḥlf 'exchange'.

In the sentence about horses producing good offspring, Fülle (abundance) is an evident slip for Füllen (foals). The Turoyo object is saxle ṭawwe, the young animals. Retain the inherited word Füllen rather than replacing it with a stylistic alternative.

before: hineinflechten, so dass immer ein Stäbchen übersprungen wird;
after: ineinanderflechten, verschränken; hineinflechten, so dass immer ein Stäbchen übersprungen wird;
rationale: The existing sheaf example shows intertwining bundles, not necessarily skipping alternating sticks. Broaden the meaning to interlacing while preserving the inherited specific weaving technique.

summary: II.1 has a zero-marked abstract object (promise, command, what is right), including the missing Preterit mxalafli. Infectum-wa at 53/27 is counterfactual, not a habitual past event.

The sheaf construction has plural affected objects and reciprocal ʕal ḥḏoḏe; its -wa form belongs in Infectum-wa. This supports a broader interlacing gloss but does not establish that every second stick is skipped in this practice.

mxalfe ne at 94/304 is a static nonmatching predicate of a pair of gaming faces. Only this predicative form is attested for the new lettered subsense; Arabic adjective versus productive Part act. remains a morphological question.
III.1 is leaving offspring, with the ant quantity in PrS86/4 beside the inherited horse example. The surface maḥləf is not silently changed to maxləf.
Is mxalfe ne at 94/304 productive II Part act. or a borrowed lexical adjective, and can finite xlf II describe nonmatching objects? The new subsense is restricted to the attested predicate.
Is ḥ for x in PrS86/4 a pronunciation, spelling convention or error? Confirm the root filing before normalizing the text.
Confirm mxalafna (69/321), particularly -na for the male dervish. Does it include an object contraction or a dialectal person ending?
The literal rose/thorn proposition is used proverbially for contrasts between mother and daughter. No independent human-offspring sense is added to II.4 or merged with III.1.
